content.tldr: The SIG Network meeting focused on triaging open issues and reviewing Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals (KEPs). Key discussions included a flaking test, a service IP routing feature request, and updates on EndpointSlice semantics and preferred close/node policies.

bullets.text: Triage of several open issues was conducted, including a flaking test, a service selector bug, and a service IP routing feature request.
Antonio highlighted the need to update the Cloud Controller Manager for accurate test results.
A KEP for TLS support in gRPC probes was discussed, with Boi potentially taking on the review.
Antonio also presented an idea for the cluster domain downward API, leveraging an OCI spec 'domain name' option.
Dan provided an update on EndpointSlice semantics, noting undocumented extensibility and potential validation issues.
Gaurav raised questions about the 'preferred close' and 'preferred node' policies for kube-proxy, prompting further review.
A flaking test for 'Signet workload balances, ETP local' was discussed, failing once a week and taking an hour.
Antonio noted the Cloud Controller Manager is outdated, affecting test accuracy.
Antonio suggested someone managing the Cloud Provider GCP needs to update it.
Boi offered to look into the Cloud Controller Manager update.
Antonio also mentioned potential impact from the DCR to AR registry migration.
A user reported a bug where a service with a named port only picked one endpoint from a pod with multiple containers.
Host explained the service assumption of fungibility, where all endpoints produce the same result.
The user was trying to collect metadata from various RPC services via a headless service, which is not currently supported.

sections.heading: Issue Triage: Kubernetes Service Cluster IP with IPN Cap IP IP

bullets.text: Antonio described a feature request for service IP routing, where traffic is routed based only on IP, losing port/protocol properties.
The user wants a service with a cluster IP only, similar to requests for old parts.
Antonio suggested it is a feature request, but the main challenge is defining the right API.
Host noted that a new API would likely require a KEP.

sections.heading: Issue Triage: Long-lived TCP connections fail

bullets.text: A user reported long-lived TCP connections failing when downscaling kube-proxy with ETP cluster.
The issue involves routing through a node that gets decommissioned without warning.
The user is not using kube-proxy's health checking to indicate node status.

sections.heading: KEP Review: TLS Support in gRPC Probe

bullets.text: Antonio brought up a KEP to add TLS support to gRPC probes, noting gRPC services often use TLS.
Boi offered to review the KEP, having historical context on gRPC probes.
The goal is to achieve parity with HTTP probes and target next alpha in 33.

sections.heading: KEP Review: Cluster Domain Downward API

bullets.text: Antonio explored using a kernel capability and IETF namespace called 'domain name' for the cluster domain downward API.
Host noted this field might be more like a NIST domain name, not DNS.
Antonio mentioned Docker uses this, implying OCI spec support, which could simplify implementation.
Host acknowledged Docker's usage reduces risk but highlighted the need for Cryo support.
Dan reported on a PR to update EndpointSlice documentation, stemming from porting the aggregated API server.
He found assumptions about EndpointSlice, like 'port' always being non-nil, were incorrect.
API server validation allows nil ports, and Kube-proxy ignores them, indicating undocumented extensibility.
Dan suggested changing some of the API if unintended.

sections.heading: KEP Review: Preferred Close vs. Preferred Node

bullets.text: Gaurav asked about the proposal to rename 'preferred close' to 'preferred same zone' and add 'preferred same node'.
Dan explained the argument is that 'preferred close' effectively means 'preferred same zone' due to implementation challenges.
Host questioned if 'prefer close' could be bent to sometimes mean 'prefer node' to avoid a new policy.
Dan stated that making 'prefer close' mean 'same node' would lead to false negatives, reverting to 'same zone'.
Gaurav will review the comments on the PR to understand the arguments better.
Boi to review the KEP for TLS support in gRPC probes.
Host to read over the service IP routing feature request and the cluster domain downward API KEP.
Host to review Dan's PR on EndpointSlice semantics and the KEP on preferred close/node.
Gaurav to review the discussion on preferred close/node policies and provide feedback.
Antonio to follow up with Cryo regarding 'domain name' support for the cluster domain downward API.

actionItems.text: Ensure the cloud controller manager is up to date for testing.
Be tagged on the cloud controller manager update issue.
Route the Cloud Controller Manager issue if needed.
Read over the 'Unable to use Kubernetes service cluster IP with IPN cap IP IP' issue.
Take the first pass at reviewing the TLS support in gRPC probe CAP.
Review the cluster domain downward API CAP.
Review Dan's PR on endpoint slice semantics documentation.
Read through the comments on the preferred close/preferred node discussion.
Review Dan's argument regarding preferred close/preferred node and provide feedback.

chapters.title: Meeting Start & Agenda
chapters.gist: The Host opened the meeting, noted the date, and mentioned a light agenda focused on CAPs and triage.

chapters.title: Issue Triage
chapters.gist: The group triaged several issues including flaking tests, service selector behavior with multiple containers, and a request for service IP routing.

chapters.title: CAP Review
chapters.gist: Antonio introduced two new CAPs: TLS support for gRPC probes and the cluster domain downward API, seeking reviewers and discussion.

chapters.title: Endpoint Slice Semantics
chapters.gist: Dan discussed challenges and assumptions found while porting the aggregated API server to endpoint slices, particularly regarding port validation.

chapters.title: Preferred Close/Node Discussion
chapters.gist: Gaurav inquired about the distinction and potential for combining 'preferred close' and 'preferred node' policies in kube-proxy.

chapters.title: Meeting Wrap-up
chapters.gist: The Host concluded the meeting early as there were no further agenda topics or discussions.
